mutant: decodeKzgG1 and decodeSetupG2: delete `if (p.is0()) throw new Error(...)`
reason: Unreachable. A point parsed from a finite compressed encoding (flag bits 100 or 101, the only ones that reach fromBytes) is never the identity; the identity encoding 0xc0 00..00 returns earlier in decodeKzgG1, and decodeSetupG2 refuses flag bits 110 in checkFiniteCompressed. The guard stays as a statement of the invariant.

Redundant with @noble/curves 1.9.7: G1.fromBytes/G2.fromBytes run the same curve and prime-order-subgroup checks and throw 'bad point: not in prime-order subgroup' themselves (the outside-subgroup test in kzg.test.ts is refused by fromBytes). The explicit call is defence in depth against a noble change; no input distinguishes the two.
batch([]) is true: every pair is the identity and is dropped by the identity filter of pairingProductIsOne (live.length === 0 returns true), so the empty set gives true with or without the guard.

mutant: domain(): delete the `if (domainCache !== undefined) return domainCache;` early return
reason: Cache only. The Domain is a deterministic function of constants; recomputing it on every call returns an identical object graph, so no verdict changes (only the time per blob).
